ruleName: RTL (Arabic) API-reference docs: a dotted-underline glossary term 'cursor' shows a hover-only tooltip on a non-focusable span that covers the curl example block. A document-level Escape handler exists but its dismiss branch is gated on document.activeElement being a text input (copied from the filter box's clear-on-Esc behavior); while hovering the term nothing is focused, so the guard is false and Escape is inert.

The Tidewater Review economics article: FOMC and bps are plain abbr title= (native, UA-controlled, out of scope / PASS), while GDP looks identical (same dotted underline) but is an abbr.gloss wrapping a span.bub author tooltip that JS reveals on hover/focus. The author bubble is pointer-events:none with no Escape handler. Two visually identical abbreviations, different owners — only the GDP one is governed by 1.4.13, and it fails; the reviewer must attribute each bubble element-by-element.

Long-form policy article: an inline glossary-term tooltip (Emissions Trading System) opens downward on hover/focus with no Esc dismiss, landing on the first ~3 lines of the next body paragraph. Method 2 absent, so Method 1 is the only path — and it obscures meaningful body text.

SaaS analytics dashboard: a '?' badge on a conversion KPI opens a definition popover that covers the device-breakdown list. The popover is hoverable and persistent, but its only dismiss affordance is a close '×' button positioned INSIDE the popover, reachable only by Tab-ing focus off the trigger and into the additional content. No Escape handler and no toggle-on-trigger.

Loom Analytics campaign dashboard: the Conversions KPI card has a focusable '?' <button> whose tooltip explains a non-obvious 7-day post-click attribution model (why the number is lower than the ad platform's 28-day count). The button is a real tab stop with aria-label, aria-describedby, and a visible focus ring, but the JS binds the reveal only to mouseover/mouseout and never to focus/focusin, so focus produces no tooltip.

Healthcare patient-portal blood-pressure intake. Side-by-side Systolic (value 118, normal) and Diastolic (value 135, out of range) number inputs. The error 'Diastolic must be between 40 and 120 mmHg.' is placed in the Systolic column under the Systolic input, and the Systolic input carries the red alert border; the out-of-range Diastolic has no message. No aria-describedby.

Online-banking transfer-limit screen: a round 'i' info button shows a tooltip on hover AND keyboard focus that overlaps the help paragraph and the Continue button. The tooltip is keyboard-reachable (meets 2.1.1) but there is NO Escape handler, no documented shortcut, and activating the trigger does not toggle it off — the only way to clear the obscuring content is to move focus/pointer off the trigger.

Telecom line-activation wizard, post-submit error state. Phone field is digits-only; the retained value is the all-digit string '12025550143'. The visible, aria-describedby-associated error reads 'Mobile number is invalid. Remove letters and parentheses from your phone number, then try again.' — describing a cause (letters/parentheses) that is factually absent from the value. The real defect (an 11-digit string for a 10-digit field) is never described.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message misidentifies the error by instructing the user to remove letters and parentheses from a phone number that contains only digits.

ruleName: Retail account signup re-displayed after a failed submit; the email field holds a malformed address (jane.summit.example.com, no @) and the sole per-field error indicator is an error icon carrying a non-empty but uselessly generic alt="error".

rubricVerdicts.summary: No input error is present or flagged for the Full name field.
The invalid email input is flagged only by visual styling and an icon with generic alt text ('error'), failing to describe the specific error in text.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the password input field.

ruleName: CONTROL / discrimination foil (PASS). Event-ticketing phone field, post-submit error state — near-identical component to case-01. The retained value is '(202) 555-CALL', which genuinely contains parentheses, a space, a dash, and the letters C-A-L-L. The field is digits-only and the visible associated error reads 'Phone number must contain only digits. Remove the letters, spaces, and parentheses (for example, enter 2025550143).' — a cause that DID occur and correctly describes this value's actual defect.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The input error is clearly identified and described in text directly beneath the field.

ruleName: PASSING counter-fixture. Higher-ed LMS reading with a '[1]' footnote reference that opens a citation popup on hover AND keyboard focus, deliberately overlapping the paragraph below (so Method 1 is not relied on). A document-level Escape handler hides the popup while focus REMAINS on the '[1]' button, and activating the trigger also toggles it closed — both SCR39-allowed dismissals.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The additional hover-revealed tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger is held and does not withdraw itself on a timer.
The hover-revealed tooltip content remains persistently visible without self-withdrawing while the trigger is hovered.

ruleName: RTL Arabic (lang=ar dir=rtl) membership address form. A 2-column x 3-row CSS grid holds Postal code (column 1, value 11564, flagged red) and City (column 2, empty). The postal-code error is placed by explicit coordinates into grid-column 2 row 3 — the City column's message slot — so on screen it sits under the empty City input. No aria-describedby.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message contradicts the field's retained value by stating that the postal code must consist of 5 digits when a 5-digit value is already present.
No input error was detected or flagged for the city field, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.

ruleName: Patient-portal medication list: an 'interactions' pill on Warfarin opens a drug-interaction warning box that covers the dosage text. An Escape handler exists but is bound to the trigger button; the trigger's own click handler calls this.blur(), moving focus to document.body, so the keydown never reaches the handler and Escape is inert while the box obscures the dose.

Banco Aurora high-yield savings page: a circular info 'i' icon next to '4.35% APY' reveals a hover-only popup disclosing a material tiered-rate caveat (4.35% only up to $250,000; above that 0.50%) found nowhere else on the page. The trigger is a non-focusable <span> with only mouseover/mouseout handlers, so keyboard, switch, and magnifier users never see the cap.

SaaS billing page: a "?" help button beside "Seat overage" shows a custom tooltip positioned 30px BELOW the trigger, separated by a transparent .gap spacer (pointer-events:none). Show/hide is bound only to the trigger button's mouseover/mouseout; the tooltip has no hover handler and is not a descendant of the trigger. Moving the pointer down to read the tooltip crosses the gap, fires mouseout, and the tooltip vanishes before the pointer reaches it.

SaaS 'set your password' screen, post-submit error state. Password field holds a 12-character value (shown as 12 bullets); the visible associated error reads 'Password must be at least 8 characters.' The page's own requirements checklist marks 'At least 8 characters' as MET (green) and 'At least one number' as the only UNMET rule (red). The error asserts a length rule already passed; the actual unmet rule (digit) triggered rejection but is not the one described, so the error contradicts the page's own checklist.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message misidentifies the validation failure by stating the password must be at least 8 characters despite the retained value meeting the length requirement.

ruleName: Pharmacy prescription page: a glossary term <dfn> ("contraindication") shows a definition pop-up that DIRECTLY overlaps/adjoins the term (top:-2px, no gap) — visually the passing arrangement the Understanding describes. But the pop-up carries pointer-events:none and reveal is keyed only to the term's :hover, so moving the pointer onto the pop-up means the cursor is no longer counted as over the term, :hover collapses, and the content vanishes. Adjacency is present but the content is not actually hoverable.

Community forum thread: a GitHub/Twitter-style profile "hover card" appears when hovering a username. It is rendered into a detached portal layer (#hovercard-layer, sibling of the content) positioned 12px below the username. Show is delayed 180ms (hover-intent); hide is immediate on the username's mouseleave; the card has no mouseenter of its own. Moving the pointer down to the card crosses the 12px transparent gap, fires mouseleave, and the card vanishes instantly.

BOUNDARY PASS. Community-garden waitlist form with stacked Full name (valid), Email (value 'priya.nair@', invalid), Phone (valid). The error 'Email address is incomplete — add the part after the @.' is rendered inside the Email field's own block directly under the Email input, which carries the red invalid border. There is NO aria-describedby — identification rests entirely on presentation, done correctly.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Full name input is not in an error state and was not rejected.
The error on the email address field is clearly identified and described in text.
The optional phone input field is not in an error state and was not rejected, so there is no error to identify.

ruleName: CONTROL (discrimination boundary): the same Riverbend Library membership flow as case-01, but the genuine SUCCESS result after VALID input (Age 34, a real email). The server accepted the data and rendered a true confirmation — a read-only summary of the accepted values, a real membership number (RVB-2026-08831), and next steps — with no editable form re-displayed and legitimately no error message. Must be judged passed while case-01..05 are failed.

Meridian Bank wire-transfer form: focusing the high-risk Amount field opens a modal security step-up dialog (role='dialog' aria-modal='true') that dims the page, moves keyboard focus to its confirm button, traps Tab, and is dismissed via Escape/Cancel. Superficially this is content appearing on focus (the 1.4.13 trigger pattern), but modal dialogs are explicitly out of scope — the correct disposition is NOT-APPLICABLE to 1.4.13 (evaluate under 3.2.1 On Focus). This is the N/A modal carve-out anchor.

Cedar Mutual Auto 3-step quote wizard silently advanced to 'Step 3 of 3, Review & buy' after an invalid ZIP ('0', too short) on Step 1 was swallowed — Step 2 (coverage options) was skipped because the rating engine had no usable ZIP. The review summary freezes the invalid ZIP '0' as read-only text and shows a placeholder premium '$—'; no error text appears. Cross-page silent-advance variant. LONG-TAIL; content-domain insurance quote wizard, APG stepper + dl review, lazy-validation persona.

E-commerce garden-seed product page with pill-badge triggers; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip with multi-sentence guidance. The auto-dismiss is implemented entirely in CSS — a @keyframes peekThenVanish animation with animation-fill-mode:forwards drives the popup to opacity:0 after ~3.5s while the badge is still hovered/focused; there is NO setTimeout/setInterval anywhere. Verified: opacity 1 at 0s -> opacity 0 at 4s while still hovering.

RTL Arabic e-commerce product page: a size-guide tooltip authored with physical left:0 does not mirror under dir=rtl and opens on top of its own trigger button, covering the label 'دليل المقاسات'. No Esc dismiss. Obscures the trigger itself — FAIL.

Healthcare new-patient intake form: a 'What's this?' help popover on the Insurance Member ID field opens down-right with no Esc dismiss and overlaps the next field's required asterisk + label (Patient date of birth) and the input being filled.

Bank reset-password screen redisplayed after rejecting a reused password; the field shows a red outline + a red CSS ::before key glyph and carries aria-invalid='true', but emits NO error text, aria-errormessage, or aria-describedby — nothing in words states what is wrong or why.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The invalid password field is indicated only through visual cues and aria-invalid without any descriptive error text.
No error was flagged or triggered for the Confirm new password field, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.

ruleName: Credit-union online-banking enrolment: red role=alert summary states 'Password must be at least 10 characters and include a number', but the Password field is valid (green, aria-invalid=false, meets the rule). The only flagged field is its sibling Confirm password (aria-invalid=true, red, 'does not match the password you entered'). The summary blames the wrong sibling and describes a different cause.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The username input is not in an error state and was not rejected, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.
The error summary misidentifies the Password field as failing length and number requirements, contradicting both its valid value and the inline confirmation status.
The error summary alert fails to identify the error on the confirm password field and incorrectly directs the user to the valid password field.

ruleName: Nonprofit one-time-gift form; the donor entered 25000 (over the stated $10,000 online maximum) and the error is conveyed by a Material-Icons-style icon-font glyph whose aria-label is the literal ligature key "error_outline" — describing the picture, not the error.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The invalid gift amount field is flagged only with a red border and a generic warning icon with the label 'error_outline', without any text identifying the specific error.
The target field ('Name on card') is not in an error state, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to it.

ruleName: Summit & Pine outdoor-gear product page (Trail Runner GTX): color swatches show the color name in a hover bubble that has no focus path (swatch:hover .hover-name, no :focus equivalent) — superficially the same failure. But the color name is already printed as a persistent visible <span> under each swatch AND is each radio's accessible name (aria-label='Pine' etc.). The hover bubble is aria-hidden and purely redundant, so the missing focus path deprives no one of additional perceivable content. Redundancy decoy → PASS.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover tooltip appears in empty space above the color swatch without obscuring or replacing any other content.
The hover-revealed tooltip fails hoverability because a physical gap separates it from the swatch trigger, extinguishing the content when the pointer moves toward it.
No hover or focus content disappears automatically on a timer while the trigger remains held.

ruleName: Alumni reunion RSVP (en-GB); email ravi@@pembury.ac.uk (double @) and date 2024-07-18 (in the past) are both invalid, but a refactor cut-and-pasted the date row's error icon above the email row without updating it, so the email field sits beside an SVG whose aria-label="Date is in the past" — correct cause for the wrong field.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Full name input field is not in an error state or flagged as invalid, so WCAG 3.3.1 does not apply to this element.
The error on the email field is not identified in text, and its programmatic error description incorrectly describes a date error instead.
The error on the preferred dinner date field is indicated only by a red border and aria-invalid without any textual error description.

ruleName: Ledgerline invoicing toolbar: every button (Save/Export/Send/Duplicate) carries only a native title= attribute (e.g. title='Save your work'). There is zero JavaScript and no author popup DOM, so the hover bubble is rendered entirely by the user agent. This is the out-of-scope boundary anchor: visually similar to the author-built failing cases, but UA-controlled and therefore inapplicable / PASS by exclusion.

Community allotment newsletter signup re-rendered after a failed submit; the invalid email field ('tom@') wears a 2px red border + red-tinted background as the SOLE error cue. No message, no aria-invalid, no hidden text anywhere conveys that an error occurred.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated for the 'Name on your library record' input field.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the 'Course you want to join' input field.
The field is visually flagged as an error solely through red border and background styling without any textual error description.

ruleName: GOV.UK council-tax reduction form: top-of-form red error summary announces 'We found 2 errors' and lists Full name + Email, but both render filled and unflagged; the only field actually in error (Telephone, value 'ring me weekdays') has a red border, inline message and aria-invalid=true and is never named. Wrong count AND wrong fields named.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error summary incorrectly identifies this field as having an error when it is not flagged or invalid.
The telephone number field is flagged in error but is omitted from the error summary block, which misdirects users by listing two unrelated valid fields instead.

ruleName: Homeware ecommerce checkout (en-GB); shipping postcode 9021 is too short and billing postcode SW1A 0AA! has an illegal character, but both reuse one SVG sprite and both <svg role=img> wrappers carry the identical hardcoded aria-label="Invalid input".

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated or flagged for the Shipping Street address field, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification is not applicable to this control.
The error on the postcode input is indicated only by a red border and a generic warning icon without identifying the error in text.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the billing street address field, so there is no error identification to evaluate.
The invalid postcode field is indicated only by a red border and a warning icon with generic label 'Invalid input', without any specific text identifying the error.

ruleName: CONTROL (discrimination boundary): auction 'place a bid' form with the IDENTICAL red border + tint on the email field, but the error is also identified and described in text ('Email address is not valid.') tied via aria-describedby, with aria-invalid='true' and the decorative icon aria-hidden. Should pass.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No input error occurred or was triggered for the 'Your name' field, making 3.3.1 error identification not applicable.
The error on the email address field is clearly identified in text and programmatically associated.
Evaluation of 3.3.1 is not applicable for the maximum bid field because no error was detected or triggered for this input.

ruleName: Home-insurance quote wizard, step 2 Property: red role=alert summary says 'Please fix 2 things: Country must be selected. Year the property was built must be a 4-digit year'. Year built is genuinely flagged (value 'nineteen eighty'), but the Country control is a disabled <select> pre-set to 'United Kingdom' (locked because the product is UK-only) — greyed, non-focusable, no aria-invalid — and could not have produced input nor be corrected.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error summary falsely identifies the disabled Country field as having an error ('Country must be selected') even though it already has a selected, fixed value.
No error was demonstrated or flagged for the Property postcode field, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this control.
The error for the property year field is clearly identified in text both directly below the field and in the error summary.

ruleName: Helios Energy kWh bar chart: each SVG rect bar has an SVG <title> child (UA-rendered native tooltip, e.g. 'February: 612 kWh', out of scope) AND an author .vtip floating overlay shown on hover with DIFFERENT, richer text ('Feb · 612 kWh · $84.10 · 18% below your 12-mo avg'). The overlay is pointer-events:none, repositions under the cursor via mousemove, and has no Escape handler. Two on-hover sources, two owners, two divergent texts — the reviewer must separate which content the SC governs (only the author overlay) and judge its behavior.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-revealed tooltip remains persistent while the trigger is hovered and does not self-withdraw on a timer.
Hover-triggered tooltip content cannot be hovered directly without being dismissed.
The hover-revealed additional content remains visible while the trigger is held and does not disappear on a timer.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists for the entire duration of the hold without withdrawing itself on a timer.
The hover-revealed tooltip directly overlaps the trigger element without any intervening gap, allowing pointer travel onto the content.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists for as long as the pointer remains on the element, satisfying the persistence requirement of WCAG 1.4.13.

ruleName: Pulsar Platform API reference (rate-limiting page): the abbreviation 'TBA' is expanded only inside a pure-CSS :hover bubble containing the load-bearing burst formula (2x rate for ~5s) stated nowhere else. The reveal is the selector abbr.term:hover .bubble with no JS, so keyboard focus structurally cannot reveal it; the author also set tabindex="-1", removing the <abbr> from the tab order.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The custom hover tooltip obscures surrounding text content and cannot be dismissed with the Escape key or any other in-place mechanism while the pointer remains over the trigger.
The hover-triggered tooltip disappears when the pointer leaves the trigger to travel onto it due to a 10px gap.
The hover-triggered tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger element is hovered and does not self-withdraw on a timer.

ruleName: University admissions application wizard, step 3 Contact details: red role=alert summary lists two G139-style jump links. Both fields (Email holding 'amara.k(at)mail', empty Telephone) are genuinely flagged, but the link labelled 'Fix your email address' has href=#phone, so activating it lands focus on the Telephone field instead of email; both links in fact point to #phone.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Preferred name input field is not in an error state and was not rejected, so error identification does not apply to this element.
The error for the email address field is not properly identified in the error summary because its summary link misdirects to the daytime telephone input.
The input error for the Daytime telephone field is clearly identified in text both inline and within the error summary.

ruleName: Real-estate listing: the entire large Walk Score hero tile is the hover/focus trigger; its explainer popover is pushed away into the next column to avoid the trigger, but lands on the Monthly cost estimate breakdown. No Esc dismiss. Tests the large-trigger 'Method 2 only' nuance.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The custom hover tooltip obscures adjacent page content and cannot be dismissed with Escape or without moving the pointer.
The hover-revealed tooltip cannot be hovered directly because moving the pointer off the trigger dismisses the content.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists indefinitely while the trigger remains hovered or focused and does not self-withdraw.

ruleName: E-commerce checkout shipping step, post-submit error state. ZIP field retains the value the user typed, '9021' (four digits). The visible associated server error reads 'ZIP code 90210 not found in our database. Please check the code and try again.' — quoting '90210', a five-digit value the user never entered (a normalizer padded a trailing zero before lookup). The real defect (ZIP too short) is never described and the quoted value contradicts the field's own retained value.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Error identification is not applicable to the Street address field because no error was flagged or demonstrated for this input.
No input error was flagged or demonstrated for the City field, making error identification inapplicable to this element.
No error was detected or flagged for the State input field.
The error message misidentifies the error by stating that 'ZIP code 90210' was not found when the retained input value is '9021'.

ruleName: E-commerce category sidebar: hovering a top-level category ("Camp & Hike") reveals a CSS-only flyout submenu offset to the right (left:230px against a 210px row, leaving a ~20px transparent corridor). The flyout is a DOM child of the category but not geometrically contiguous; reaching lower submenu items requires a diagonal down-and-right path that exits both hot-zones, ending the :hover state and collapsing the flyout before the cursor arrives.

Government SNAP-benefits two-column grid form. Row 1 has First name (left, filled 'Maria') and Last name (right, filled). After a failed submit the error 'First name is required.' is placed in the right-column cell directly under the Last name input, and Last name (not First name) gets aria-invalid=true. No aria-describedby links the message to any control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message 'First name is required.' is placed beneath and associated with the 'Last (family) name' input rather than the target 'First (given) name' input.
The error text misidentifies the field in error by stating 'First name is required' beneath the flagged 'Last (family) name' field.
No input error was flagged or demonstrated for the Middle initial field.
No input error occurred or was flagged for the optional 'Preferred name' field.

ruleName: Healthcare new-patient intake, post-submit error state. Date-of-birth field retains '03/14/2027', which already conforms exactly to MM/DD/YYYY. The visible associated error reads 'Date of birth is invalid. Please use the MM/DD/YYYY format.' — naming a constraint that is already satisfied. The actual error (a birth date set in the future) is never described, so the only guidance is a no-op fix.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No input error was detected or demonstrated for the Legal name field.
The error message misidentifies the problem by claiming the date format is invalid when the input already conforms to MM/DD/YYYY.

ruleName: CONTROL (passing): flight-booking Passenger details step. Red role=alert summary states 'There are 2 problems' and lists exactly two G139 jump links — Email (→#email) and Date of birth (→#dob). The page flags exactly those two fields with matching aria-invalid, anchors, and inline message wording; the two valid fields (Given names, Passport number) are correctly not mentioned. Count, membership, link targets, and wording all reconcile.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The 'Given names' field is not in error, so error identification requirements do not apply to it.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the Passport number field, so error identification does not apply to this element.
The error for the email address field is clearly identified in text both inline and within the error summary.
The date of birth input error is clearly identified and described in text both inline and in the page error summary.

ruleName: E-commerce checkout payment row (Card number / Expiry / CVV) in a flex row. The CVV value '12' is the truly-invalid input, but the error 'CVV must be exactly 3 digits.' is rendered in the message slot under the Card number field, and the Card number input carries the red invalid border. No aria-describedby anywhere.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Card number field is marked in an error state but displays an error message referencing the CVV field instead.
No error was demonstrated for the Expiry field.
The error message for the invalid CVV input is misplaced under the Card Number field, leaving the CVV field unflagged and lacking associated error text.

ruleName: Restaurant catering-enquiry form: red role=alert summary lists three errors (Event date, City, Number of guests). Event date and Number of guests are genuinely flagged below, but the middle line 'City is required' names a field that does not exist anywhere on the form — the page collects a single free-text 'Venue name & full address' textarea with no City input, label, or control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error for the Event date field is clearly identified in text both inline and within the error summary.
No error was demonstrated for the venue address textarea, as it is valid and not flagged in error.
The error for the Number of guests field is clearly and accurately identified in text both inline and within the error summary.

ruleName: SaaS analytics cohort-retention grid with dotted-underline column-header terms; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip definition. A scroll listener on the fixed-height, sticky-header scroller hides the popup the moment the user nudges the grid to read a lower row, although hover on the term is retained. Verified: visible before scroll -> hidden after scrollTop change.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-triggered tooltip remains visible for the entire duration the trigger is held without self-withdrawing on a timer.
The hover-revealed tooltip remains visible while the trigger is held and does not disappear on a timer.

ruleName: Folio & Thread e-commerce checkout (Step 3 of 3, Payment) bounced after the gateway rejected a 13-digit card number ('4716 1234 5678 9', too short) and empty CVC; the theme injected a green role=status banner 'Thank you — your order is being processed' above the re-displayed payment form with the invalid card retained. Variant B (mismatched success banner). HEAD-prevalence; content-domain e-commerce/checkout, Shopify-Dawn-style theme.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No client-side validation error surfaced upon form submission, leaving server-side error identification inconclusive.
No error state could be observed or induced on the card number field, leaving error identification inconclusive.
No input error was triggered, flagged at rest, or surfaced client-side for the expiry field.
No input error was presented or triggered for the security code field.

ruleName: Online-banking add-payee; the German IBAN DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 0X ends in an illegal X and is invalid (red border), but a Vue state-merge bug left the field's status SVG at its initial success state: a green check with <title>Looks good!</title> — an inverted text alternative.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated or flagged for the Payee name field.
The invalid IBAN field is marked with a red border and aria-invalid but provides no text identifying the error.

ruleName: Conference call-for-papers form returned after a blank required 'Talk title'; the only error/required cue is the label turned red with a trailing CSS ::after asterisk. No message, no legend explaining the asterisk, no required/aria-required/aria-invalid.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated or flagged for the Full name field.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the Date of birth field.

ruleName: CONTROL (passes): government heating-assistance application; the email carla.mendes#state.gov uses # instead of @ and the error icon carries a correct, specific alt="Email address must contain an @ symbol — for example, name@example.com", echoed by a linked error summary.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was detected or flagged for the applicant name field.
The input error is clearly and accurately identified in text both in the top error summary and via programmatic association.
No error was detected or flagged for the phone number field.

ruleName: Healthcare new-patient registration: red role=alert summary declares 'There is 1 error in this form' and lists only Date of birth, but three fields render red with inline messages and aria-invalid=true — Date of birth (invalid date), Mobile number (too short), and Postcode (invalid). The summary undercounts the real error state by two and omits two flagged fields.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No input error was flagged or demonstrated for the First name field, making WCAG 3.3.1 error identification inapplicable to this element.
The error for the Date of birth field is accurately identified in text both inline and within the summary.
The error summary announces only 1 error (Date of birth) and omits the invalid Mobile number field.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the Address line 1 input, making error identification for this field not applicable.

ruleName: French bistro reservation form re-rendered after no seating choice was made; the required radio group is flagged ONLY by reddening its <legend> ('Préférence de salle'). No text says a choice is required or that the group errored; no aria-required/aria-invalid.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was triggered or demonstrated for the reservation name field.
No error was triggered or demonstrated for the date input field.

ruleName: Government parking-permit form: a "?" help tooltip beside the "Parking zone" select, built correctly as the PASS anchor on the same component family. The tooltip is adjacent/overlapping (4px overlap, no gap), has pointer-events:auto and its own mouseenter, a 120ms hide delay tolerates the sub-element transition, and Esc dismisses it.
